title: The Last Bench
protagonist: Corwin Brandvold, planning engineer at Quartz Mesa (fictional open-pit gold mine outside the fictional town of Ebbet Wells) [CONSTRUCTED]
primary_metric: life-of-pit cash margin, undiscounted, in USD million

options.A: Close at the Floor: mine out only the planned reserve (25 Mt ore + 50 Mt waste) and close the pit
options.B: The Sixty-Meter Pushback: widen and deepen the pit by 60 m to reach the next block of ore, on top of the same planned reserve

reinforcement_note: Checked 2026-10-28 against readmodel/standards_spine.json. All 10 claimed skills already have n>=2 (geometry-cone n=3 from The Enclosure Call/The Custom Die/Fizzer Order; geometry-cylinder n=3; volume-of-a-cone n=2 from The Cooling Curve/Fizzer Order; volume-of-a-cylinder n=2 from Nuclear Waste/The Painted Gallon; the other six n=4..90). The only spine skills with n<=1 are Digit, divide-a-fraction-by-a-fraction, pentagon/heptagon/nonagon/decagon/dodecagon/N-gon, missing-data-element-from-the-mean, box-and-whisker plot, and the calculus chain/quotient-rule, volume-of-revolution/disk-method and Taylor-series skills; none is reachable from D1-D5 (the pit and pipe are cones and a cylinder, not revolved solids or polygons; no mean, box plot or fraction division is asked for). The other Geometry Surface Area And Volume skills (prism, pyramid, sphere) are n=2 or 3 and are not forced either. Tan(42 degrees) was considered and rejected: claiming pre-calculus-tangent-function would require students to compute the rim radii, moving the case to T4; the radii are given. This is an honest reinforcement case: it thickens two n=2 'how to' holes (cone and cylinder volume) from a new domain (mining), it does not manufacture a skill the deliverables do not force.

sources.claim: Definitions of bench and stripping ratio
sources.value: Bench: ledge forming a single level of operation from which mineral or waste is mined. Stripping ratio: waste removed per unit of ore.
sources.title: Open Pit Fundamentals (MAD455 lecture notes); Stripping ratio
sources.note: University lecture notes (fetched, text confirmed: 'BENCH: Ledge that forms a single level of operation...'; 'Stripping ratio refers to the ratio of the volume of overburden (or waste material) required to be removed to the volume of ore recovered'; also defines cutoff stripping ratio as the ratio where mining cost of ore and waste is matched by revenue). Wikipedia 'Strip ratio' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strip_ratio) confirms 'amount of waste (or overburden) that must be removed to release a given ore quantity'. Context only; no graded quantity.

_ext: keys below are pipeline extensions, additive to SPEC section 4

deliverables.text: A pit volume table: current-design and post-pushback pit volumes as large cone minus small floor cone (Mm3), the pushback shell in Mm3 and Mt, a second-method check, and why the floor cone does not affect the shell.
An ore-pipe and stripping table: pipe cylinder volume (Mm3), tonnage (Mt), troy ounces recovered, waste tonnes in the shell, stripping ratio, with every unit conversion shown.

A cash-margin table at the planning price with the margin stated as (winner - loser)/winner in percent, and each option's cash margin as an equation in gold price P solved algebraically for the break-even price.
A stake table: mine life, crew-years for each option, extra crew-years, forgone cash per extra crew-year, crew as a percent of town population.
An original visual: the two cash-margin lines against gold price, the four USGS annual prices plotted, the break-even marked.

extensions_optional: E1 stripping ratio vs break-even stripping ratio for 2021-2024
E2 rerun D4 with own crew or throughput
E3 discounting test using the MA7 convention

balance.argument_a: At the 2024 planning price (2,388 USD/oz) each ore tonne nets 45.56 USD after processing, but the pushback moves 146.6 Mt of rock to uncover 9.61 Mt of ore (stripping ratio 14.26, above the 12.11 break-even), so it loses 1.9 USD million before capital and 62.0 USD million after. A earns the higher cash margin, 914.1 vs 852.1 USD million, with no capital at risk.
balance.argument_b: The break-even gold price is about 2,616 USD/oz, 9.6% above the planning price, in a USGS series that rose 32.6% from 2021 to 2024. The pushback adds 271.8 koz of recoverable gold and extends mine life from 3.75 to 11.08 years: 1,319 extra crew-years for about 47,000 USD of forgone cash each.
balance.margin_basis: (winner - loser)/winner on undiscounted life-of-pit cash margin at the 2024 USGS price: A wins by 62.0 / 914.1.
balance.sensitivity: The verdict is not stable under +/-50% of many scenario assumptions (flip points listed in FACILITATOR.md and sensitivity_disclosure[]); the case discloses this rather than hiding it. Metric convention in this case is gap / winner (6.78%); tier2_probes.py reports the same gap as gap / loser (7.3%).

Flips the winner at +9.6%. Disclosed in FACILITATOR.md; Category X is the closest bucket, human acceptance of the mapping needed.

sensitivity_note: SPEC section 6 facilitator note: the case concerns a mine closing and a crew losing work in a small town. Students may have family in mining, energy or another closed industry. The crew and town figures are a scenario the class may change, not a prediction. Ask who bears the cost of each option without blaming a person; do not let the cash margin alone end the debate, and make the math show the stake rather than assume it.

cohort_bands.note: The 45-minute Socratic plan in FACILITATOR.md runs as written, with two or three deep-conflict threads at 20:00-30:00 (cash margin vs crew-years; a one-year price estimate vs an irreversible commitment; who bears the cost).

Anchors 2 and 3 combine into one pass. The twist still drops at 15:00 but only one deep-conflict thread runs (cash margin vs crew-years); the other threads fold into the close. Total runtime shortens proportionally.

No vote to take: Anchor 1 becomes a stated initial position. The guide plays devil's advocate directly, arguing the option the learner did not choose. The twist still lands, but 'who reverses' becomes 'would you reverse, and why'.

context_glossary.desc: One working level of an open-pit mine, like a giant stair step, from which rock is dug.
A planned expansion of an open pit: a zone outside the current pit that is dug as one operation, widening and deepening the hole.
How many tonnes of waste rock must be dug out to reach one tonne of ore.
The amount of gold per tonne in the ore as it arrives at the processing plant, here measured in grams per tonne.
Rock that contains too little gold to be worth processing but has to be moved to get at the ore.
The unit gold is priced in; one troy ounce is a little over 31 grams.
